description.narrative:
The MyTank Project, implemented in Kisima Ward, Meru County, Kenya, has achieved significant results in its first year (March 2024May 2025), addressing water scarcity, food security, and community resilience.
The MyTank Project has successfully met its year 1 targets by installing 150 water tanks, distributing 1,200 avocado seedlings, and training beneficiaries, directly improving water access and reduced average walking time to water sources from 30 minutes to 5 minutes, alleviating the burden of water fetching, particularly for women. Households now have reliable access to clean water for domestic use, farming, and livestock. By the second quarter of Year 2, the foundation had achieved 63% (95/150) of the yearly full installation target. Active installations are concentrated in Kisima and Subuiga, while Kamiti carried over from Year 1. Key activities included a feedback workshop with Year 1 beneficiaries and comprehensive avocado training for Year 2 beneficiaries. Primary challenges remain the delay in beneficiary payments and slower-than-expected fund disbursement, which have pushed completion timeline to February 2026. Health, and agricultural potential for vulnerable households - While avocado trees are not yet mature, the project anticipates an annual fruit yield of 2050 kg per household starting in year 3, laying the foundation for future income generation and improved nutrition and households being better equipped to adapt to climate variability.
Unexpected challenges, such as community tensions and technical adjustments, provided valuable lessons for future phases, while high beneficiary engagement underscored the project's resilience. These results align with SDGs 1, 2, 5, 6, and 13, demonstrating a holistic approach to rural development. While not a positive outcome, this highlighted the need for broader community engagement and transparent communication.
Future efforts will focus on upscaling to underserved areas, enhancing monitoring, and strengthening climate education to sustain and amplify impact locally.
